title: Bennie Moten's band splits and Thamon Hayes forms the Rockets
summary: After the Moten band split, Thamon Hayes took half and formed what became the Kansas City Rockets; Dickenson left for Cincinnati and Clarence Page's band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So the guys remembered me, and they...there was... They had some kind of a thing going on where the guys was

fighting each other or something -- you know, disagreeing -- in the Bennie Moten band. So they...they split. Half of them went one way, and half went the other. The one that went...that wasn't...that didn't stay with Bennie was Thamon Hayes. He took the band, Thamon Hayes. And we stayed together for a little while. This band later turned out to be the Rockets, the Kansas City Rockets.
Yes. Harlan was in the band, but he wasn't in...he didn't have...it wasn't his band at first.

Yeah, Thamon Hayes. And then I left the band and came back to Cincinnati, and played with Fats Waller and... Well, Fats had a guy to get the band together. His name was Clarence Page. So I played with Clarence Page. He just died, incidentally, about two months ago now. He had an album of pictures that's... Boy, it's the best album I've ever seen. I was a very good friend of his. His wife promised to give me that album. You know, I wanted it. There's pictures of all the guys, you know, from way back -- Midwest bands and things. I've just got to get that album, you know.
